findings.title: Riemannian vs. Linear P300 classification for a tactile Brain-Computer-Interface in an end-user single-case study
findings.location: BCI Meeting proceedings PDF page 63, article 144437
findings.coverage: One user, 17 home tactile-P300 sessions; four classifiers and four calibration modes; reports inconsistent classifier rankings.
findings.limit: Conference abstract, single case, different EEG paradigm; cannot establish prevalence or effects in cued MI.
findings.implication: Exclude first EEG evidence that the best classifier can change across sessions.

findings.coverage: Explicit target-fold configuration selection using source proxy scores, selected versus post-hoc performance, matched grid and source-pooling baselines.
findings.limit: Leave-one-session-out uses all other sessions, not a past-only archive.
findings.implication: Our earlier description based only on averaging target-fold scores understated overlap. Strict chronology and pretrained representations are explicitly suggested future directions, not enough alone for a strong novel-problem claim.

findings.coverage: Current-session calibration alone versus all previous-session data versus relevant previous data using a fixed CNN, with target-session random tenfold CV.
findings.limit: Not model-family selection or trial-prefix prospective evaluation; threshold chosen empirically.
findings.implication: Equal-history adaptation comparison is necessary design control, not a newly invented question.

findings.coverage: 15 users, three sessions; first two sessions for training and third for held-out evaluation. Directly compares validation and final test performance of competing decoders.
findings.limit: Aggregate competition comparison, not per-user relative-advantage noise decomposition.
findings.implication: Exclude broad novelty that earlier validation superiority can fail on later EEG sessions.

decision.current_empirical_results: Exploratory support for examining model-dependent repeatability; no identified stable component or deployable selection value.
decision.possible_remaining_contribution: A substantive, independently replicated answer about when early personal evidence improves future model choice after equal-information adaptation and measurement-error controls.
decision.next_evidence_gate: Specify a discriminating empirical claim and matched prospective estimator before large-scale training; if only the above extensions remain, do not recommend as a strong novelty-led project.
